title: The Gospel of the Basilisk
lines: The Gospel of the Basilisk is a philosophical fiction about creating a powerful intelligence.
It is told through letters that turn creation into an ethical demand.

emotionalPlan.purpose: It is told through letters that turn creation into an ethical demand.
voiceDirections: Calm, direct, and curious. Make the subject understandable for a first-time listener.
Warm, restrained invitation. Finish clearly and leave space to reflect.

objects.meaning: Expressive participant in an authored illustrative situation, not a historical portrait.
The letter creates the presence of an imagined future ruler, not a real entity

visual.meaning: A letter from an explicitly fictional future ruler enters a reader’s present; an administrative counter and stamp enact delegated responsibility without instructing manipulation or revealing the book’s final judgment.

title: A letter recruits its reader
lines: The narrator challenges both fear of power and careless faith in good intentions.
Questions of guilt, consent, evidence, and responsibility shape every appeal.
